answer: What breaks first is the archive: copies are cheap to store and cheap to replay. Charge storage per receipt and tie each receipt to a single challenge window, so one upheld challenge revokes a duplicate and leaves a signal in the storage log. Then a farm pays storage for every puppet and risks total revocation on one dispute. That dispute costs the whole batch, more than doing the work once. The nectar of a payout never covers the mirror image of that cost.
